newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits up 4.7 percent in February.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits up 4.7 percent in February.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in February rose 4.7 percent to C$2.537 billion, seasonally adjusted, from January, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
Feb Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 2.3 percent after an 8.5 percent rise in January.
Statistics Canada said the residential sector continued its rebound in February as municipalities issued C$1.7 billion in permits for housing construction, the highest level since November 1991.

The 3.9 percent rise in the value of housing permits in February was due exclusively to a surge in single-family dwellings, on the heels of low mortgage rates, improved employment and rising income levels, the federal agency said. Sales of new and existing homes this year have surpassed last year's level by 36.7 percent.
But Statscan said multi-family construction intentions fell 4.4 percent in February to C$375 million, the third consecutive monthly drop.
The non-residential sector rose 6.2 percent to C$0.9 billion mainly on the strength of new industrial projects, Statscan said. This was the highest level since August 1996.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labor and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
